title: Glossary
markdown:
## A–C
| Term | Plain English | Learn it in |
|---|---|---|
| **ABI** | The binary-level contract between compiled pieces (layouts, name mangling, calling conventions) | [[13.08 Idioms and Design Patterns]] |
| **Abstract class** | A class with at least one pure virtual function; can't be created directly | [[8.05 Abstract Classes and Interfaces]] |
| **ADL** | Argument-dependent lookup: functions are also searched in the namespaces of the arguments' types | [[13.07 Name Lookup ADL and the ODR]] |
| **Aggregate** | A simple struct/array you can brace-initialize member by member | [[4.06 Structs]] |
| **Alignment** | The address multiple a type must be stored at | [[13.02 Memory Layout Unions and Bit Fields]] |
| **Allocator** | An object that supplies memory to a container | [[13.03 Allocators Placement new and PMR]] |
| **Argument** | The actual value passed in a function call | [[1.07 Functions Basics]] |
| **Assertion** | A debug check that crashes loudly if a "can't happen" condition occurs | [[3.07 Input Validation and assert]] |
| **Atomic** | An operation no other thread can see half-done | [[12.05 Atomics and the Memory Model]] |
| **Big-O** | How work grows as input grows | [[5.11 Sorting Searching and Timing]] |
| **Binding (early/late)** | Choosing which function to call at compile time vs runtime | [[8.04 How Virtual Works - vtables]] |
| **Cache line** | The 64-byte chunk memory moves in | [[13.04 Performance and Cache-Friendly Code]] |
| **Capture** | Outside variables a lambda can use | [[5.07 Lambdas]] |
| **Class** | A user-defined type bundling data with functions | [[6.01 Classes and Objects]] |
| **Compiler** | Translates source code into machine code | [[1.01 How C++ Works]] |
| **Composition** | An object owns its parts ("has-a") | [[7.07 Object Relationships]] |
| **Concept** | A named compile-time requirement on a template type | [[9.04 Concepts]] |
| **const** | Can't be changed after initialization | [[2.06 const and constexpr]] |
| **constexpr / consteval** | Can / must be computed at compile time | [[11.04 Compile-Time Programming]] |
| **Constructor** | Function that sets up a new object | [[6.02 Constructors]] |
| **Coroutine** | A function that can pause and resume | [[12.07 Coroutines]] |
| **CRTP** | `class D : Base<D>` — compile-time polymorphism trick | [[11.05 CRTP and Static Polymorphism]] |
| **CTAD** | The compiler deduces a class template's arguments | [[9.01 Class Templates]] |

## D–I
| Term | Plain English | Learn it in |
|---|---|---|
| **Dangling** | A pointer/reference to something that no longer exists | [[4.03 References]] |
| **Data race** | Two threads touch the same data, one writes, no sync → UB | [[12.02 Mutexes and Locks]] |
| **Deadlock** | Threads waiting on each other forever | [[12.02 Mutexes and Locks]] |
| **Declaration / definition** | "This exists" vs "here's what it is" | [[1.08 Multiple Files and Headers]] |
| **Deep copy** | Copying the data a pointer refers to, not just the pointer | [[7.03 Copy Semantics]] |
| **Dereference** | Follow a pointer to the value (`*p`) | [[4.04 Pointers]] |
| **Destructor** | Function that cleans up when an object dies | [[6.03 Destructors and Object Lifetime]] |
| **Encapsulation** | Hiding data behind a public interface | [[6.01 Classes and Objects]] |
| **Enum class** | A scoped, type-safe list of named values | [[4.05 Enums]] |
| **Exception** | An object thrown to signal an error up the call stack | [[9.05 Exceptions]] |
| **Expression** | Code that produces a value | [[1.06 Operators and Expressions Basics]] |
| **Fold expression** | Apply an operator across a parameter pack | [[9.03 Variadic Templates and Fold Expressions]] |
| **Forwarding reference** | `T&&` in a template; binds to anything | [[11.01 Value Categories and Perfect Forwarding]] |
| **Functor** | An object callable like a function (`operator()`) | [[6.08 Operator Overloading Advanced]] |
| **Future** | A handle to a result that will arrive later | [[12.04 Futures Promises and async]] |
| **Header** | A file of declarations you `#include` | [[1.08 Multiple Files and Headers]] |
| **Heap (free store)** | Memory you request at runtime | [[7.01 Stack vs Heap]] |
| **Inheritance** | A class built on another ("is-a") | [[8.01 Inheritance Basics]] |
| **Inline** | May be defined in multiple files identically (ODR-safe) | [[3.06 Global Variables and Linkage]] |
| **Instantiation** | The compiler stamping out a template for specific types | [[4.02 Function Templates]] |
| **Invariant** | A rule that must always hold for an object | [[6.09 Designing Good Classes]] |
| **Iterator** | A cursor pointing into a container | [[5.06 Iterators and Algorithms]] |

## L–R
| Term | Plain English | Learn it in |
|---|---|---|
| **Lambda** | An inline anonymous function | [[5.07 Lambdas]] |
| **Leak** | Memory allocated but never freed | [[7.02 new and delete]] |
| **Linkage** | Whether a name is visible to other .cpp files | [[3.06 Global Variables and Linkage]] |
| **Linker** | Joins compiled files and libraries into one program | [[1.01 How C++ Works]] |
| **Literal** | A value written directly in code (`42`, `"hi"`) | [[2.02 Integers]] |
| **lvalue / rvalue** | Has a name/address vs a temporary | [[7.05 Move Semantics]] |
| **Memory order** | Rules for what other threads see and when | [[12.05 Atomics and the Memory Model]] |
| **Module** | Modern replacement for headers (`import`) | [[13.05 Modules]] |
| **Move** | Steal resources from an object that's done with them | [[7.05 Move Semantics]] |
| **Mutex** | A lock letting one thread at a time into code | [[12.02 Mutexes and Locks]] |
| **Namespace** | A named group of names (`std::`) | [[3.05 Scope Lifetime and Namespaces]] |
| **noexcept** | Promise that a function won't throw | [[9.06 Exception Safety and noexcept]] |
| **nullptr** | The "points to nothing" pointer value | [[4.04 Pointers]] |
| **ODR** | One Definition Rule — define things once (or identically) | [[13.07 Name Lookup ADL and the ODR]] |
| **Overloading** | Same function name, different parameters | [[4.01 Overloading and Default Arguments]] |
| **Override** | Derived class replaces a virtual function | [[8.03 Virtual Functions]] |
| **Parameter** | The variable in a function definition | [[1.07 Functions Basics]] |
| **pImpl** | Hide a class's internals behind a pointer | [[13.08 Idioms and Design Patterns]] |
| **Placement new** | Construct an object in memory you already have | [[13.03 Allocators Placement new and PMR]] |
| **Pointer** | A variable holding a memory address | [[4.04 Pointers]] |
| **Polymorphism** | One interface, many behaviours | [[8.03 Virtual Functions]] |
| **Preprocessor** | Text-substitution step before compiling (`#include`, `#define`) | [[13.06 Preprocessor and Attributes]] |
| **RAII** | Tie resources to object lifetimes | [[7.04 RAII and the Rule of Three]] |
| **Range / view** | Something you can iterate; a lazy, non-owning range adaptor | [[10.03 Ranges and Views]] |
| **Recursion** | A function calling itself on a smaller problem | [[5.09 Recursion]] |
| **Reference** | An alias for an existing variable | [[4.03 References]] |
| **Rule of 0/3/5** | Special member functions come as a set — ideally none | [[7.05 Move Semantics]] |

## S–Z
| Term | Plain English | Learn it in |
|---|---|---|
| **Scope** | Where in code a name is visible | [[3.05 Scope Lifetime and Namespaces]] |
| **SFINAE** | Bad template substitution removes an overload instead of erroring | [[11.03 SFINAE and enable_if]] |
| **Shadowing** | Inner variable hides an outer one with the same name | [[3.05 Scope Lifetime and Namespaces]] |
| **Short-circuit** | `&&`/`\|\|` skip the right side when the answer is known | [[2.08 Operators Deep Dive]] |
| **Slicing** | Copying a derived object into a base object loses the derived part | [[8.06 Slicing, Casting and Composition]] |
| **Smart pointer** | RAII pointer that deletes automatically | [[7.06 Smart Pointers]] |
| **Specialization** | Custom template version for specific arguments | [[9.02 Advanced Templates]] |
| **Stack** | Fast automatic memory for locals and calls | [[7.01 Stack vs Heap]] |
| **Stack unwinding** | Destroying locals while an exception propagates | [[9.05 Exceptions]] |
| **Static** | Lives for the whole program / belongs to the class / file-private | [[6.05 Static Members and Friends]] |
| **Statement** | One instruction ending in `;` | [[1.03 Anatomy of a Program]] |
| **STL** | The standard containers, iterators and algorithms | [[10.01 Choosing STL Containers]] |
| **Strict aliasing** | You may not read an object through an unrelated pointer type | [[13.01 Undefined Behavior and Object Lifetime]] |
| **Template** | A recipe that generates code for any type | [[4.02 Function Templates]] |
| **this** | Pointer to the object a member function was called on | [[6.04 this and const Member Functions]] |
| **Thread** | An independent path of execution | [[12.01 Threads and jthread]] |
| **Translation unit** | A .cpp file after preprocessing — what the compiler compiles | [[1.08 Multiple Files and Headers]] |
| **Type erasure** | Hide different types behind one value-type interface | [[11.06 Type Erasure]] |
| **Type trait** | Compile-time question/transform about a type | [[11.02 Type Traits]] |
| **Undefined behavior (UB)** | Code with no defined meaning — anything can happen | [[13.01 Undefined Behavior and Object Lifetime]] |
| **Variadic template** | Template taking any number of arguments | [[9.03 Variadic Templates and Fold Expressions]] |
| **Variant** | Holds exactly one of several types | [[10.04 optional variant and tuple]] |
| **Virtual function** | Called based on the object's real type at runtime | [[8.03 Virtual Functions]] |
| **vtable** | Per-class table of virtual function addresses | [[8.04 How Virtual Works - vtables]] |
